item.vignette: An 18-year-old woman has had bilateral renal cysts since childhood and persistent hypomagnesemia due to renal magnesium wasting. She now develops nonautoimmune diabetes mellitus. MRI shows pancreatic hypoplasia and a bicornuate uterus. Her mother has chronic kidney disease and diabetes diagnosed at age 28. Urinalysis shows no hematuria and minimal proteinuria.
item.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this patient's findings?

options.A: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to MUC1
options.D: HNF1B-related disease (renal cysts and diabetes/MODY5 spectrum)

item.tested_construct: HNF1B haploinsufficiency causes a multisystem developmental disorder in which renal cystic/structural disease commonly coexists with renal magnesium wasting, pancreatic abnormalities, early-onset nonautoimmune diabetes, and genital-tract malformations.

explanation.key_explanation: The combination of renal cysts, renal magnesium wasting, pancreatic hypoplasia, nonautoimmune diabetes, genital-tract malformation, and autosomal-dominant family history is characteristic of HNF1B-related disease. HNF1B is a developmental transcription factor required in kidney, pancreas, liver, and genitourinary organogenesis.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to MUC1'. It is not selected because it does not account for the syndromic combination of renal cysts, renal magnesium wasting, pancreatic hypoplasia, nonautoimmune diabetes, and a Müllerian anomaly; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'Branchio-oto-renal syndrome due to EYA1'. It is not selected because it does not account for the syndromic combination of renal cysts, renal magnesium wasting, pancreatic hypoplasia, nonautoimmune diabetes, and a Müllerian anomaly; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'PAX2-related papillorenal syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for the syndromic combination of renal cysts, renal magnesium wasting, pancreatic hypoplasia, nonautoimmune diabetes, and a Müllerian anomaly; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. The combination of renal cysts, renal magnesium wasting, pancreatic hypoplasia, nonautoimmune diabetes, genital-tract malformation, and autosomal-dominant family history is characteristic of HNF1B-related disease. HNF1B is a developmental transcription factor required in kidney, pancreas, liver, and genitourinary organogenesis.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Gitelman syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for the syndromic combination of renal cysts, renal magnesium wasting, pancreatic hypoplasia, nonautoimmune diabetes, and a Müllerian anomaly; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize HNF1B-related disease from the syndromic combination of renal structural disease, hypomagnesemia, pancreatic abnormalities, nonautoimmune diabetes, and genital-tract malformations.

item.vignette: An 11-year-old boy is evaluated for progressive mixed hearing loss. Examination shows bilateral preauricular pits and a small draining fistula along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Renal ultrasonography shows unilateral renal hypoplasia. item.vignette: A 39-year-old man has slowly progressive chronic kidney disease with a bland urine sediment and minimal proteinuria. His father and paternal grandmother reached kidney failure in middle age. Kidney size is normal to mildly reduced without a dominant cystic pattern. Long-read sequencing identifies a frameshift mutation within the variable-number tandem-repeat region of MUC1.
item.lead_in: Which cellular consequence most directly causes this patient's kidney disease?

options.A: Misfolded uromodulin accumulates in the endoplasmic reticulum of thick ascending limb cells
options.B: Loss of nephrin disrupts the podocyte slit diaphragm
options.C: Defective primary-cilium signaling causes corticomedullary cyst formation
options.D: Loss of type IV collagen destabilizes the glomerular basement membrane
options.E: A toxic frameshifted MUC1 protein accumulates in tubular epithelial cells

item.tested_construct: ADTKD-MUC1 is caused by MUC1 VNTR frameshift mutations that generate a toxic frameshifted MUC1 protein (MUC1fs), producing progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease.

explanation.key_explanation: The explicitly identified MUC1 VNTR frameshift points to ADTKD-MUC1. These variants produce an abnormal frameshifted MUC1 protein that is toxic to kidney tubular cells; this is distinct from UMOD-associated endoplasmic-reticulum retention of mutant uromodulin.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Misfolded uromodulin accumulates in the endoplasmic reticulum of thick ascending limb cells'. It is not selected because it does not account for the documented MUC1 VNTR frameshift together with autosomal-dominant bland progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'Loss of nephrin disrupts the podocyte slit diaphragm'. It is not selected because it does not account for the documented MUC1 VNTR frameshift together with autosomal-dominant bland progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Defective primary-cilium signaling causes corticomedullary cyst formation'. It is not selected because it does not account for the documented MUC1 VNTR frameshift together with autosomal-dominant bland progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Loss of type IV collagen destabilizes the glomerular basement membrane'. It is not selected because it does not account for the documented MUC1 VNTR frameshift together with autosomal-dominant bland progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. The explicitly identified MUC1 VNTR frameshift points to ADTKD-MUC1. These variants produce an abnormal frameshifted MUC1 protein that is toxic to kidney tubular cells; this is distinct from UMOD-associated endoplasmic-reticulum retention of mutant uromodulin.

item.vignette: A 29-year-old man has progressive exertional dyspnea. Chest CT shows innumerable bilateral calcified micronodules with a dense “sandstorm” appearance despite relatively mild symptoms. Serum calcium, phosphate, and parathyroid hormone levels are normal. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC34A2.
item.lead_in: Which physiologic defect most directly produces the pulmonary deposits?

options.A: Reduced chloride secretion through CFTR in airway epithelial cells
options.B: Failure to load surfactant phospholipids into lamellar bodies
options.C: Reduced phosphate uptake from the alveolar space by a type IIb sodium-phosphate cotransporter, promoting calcium-phosphate microlith formation
options.D: Unopposed neutrophil elastase activity due to reduced alpha-1 antitrypsin
options.E: Failure of surfactant protein B to spread phospholipids at the air-liquid interface

item.tested_construct: SLC34A2 encodes the type IIb sodium-phosphate cotransporter; loss of function causes pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis with accumulation of calcium-phosphate microliths in alveoli.

explanation.key_explanation: Pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis is caused by inactivating SLC34A2 variants. Impaired alveolar phosphate transport permits local phosphate accumulation and precipitation with calcium, forming characteristic intra-alveolar microliths.

It is not selected because it does not account for biallelic SLC34A2 loss with diffuse calcium-phosphate alveolar microliths despite normal systemic calcium-phosphate studies; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.

item.vignette: A term newborn develops severe respiratory distress within hours of birth and requires prolonged mechanical ventilation. Cultures are negative, echocardiography excludes major structural heart disease, and testing for SFTPB and SFTPC variants is negative. Electron microscopy of type II pneumocytes shows abnormal dense lamellar bodies. Sequencing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in ABCA3.
item.lead_in: Which normal cellular function is most directly impaired?

options.A: Clearance of phosphate from the alveolar space by a sodium-phosphate cotransporter
options.B: Transport and packaging of surfactant phospholipids into lamellar bodies of type II pneumocytes
options.C: Apical chloride secretion by airway epithelial CFTR channels
options.D: Proteolytic activation of surfactant protein C after secretion
options.E: Assembly of elastic fibers in the pulmonary interstitium

item.tested_construct: ABCA3 is a phospholipid transporter in type II pneumocytes required for transport and organization of surfactant lipids within lamellar bodies; loss of function causes severe neonatal surfactant dysfunction or later interstitial lung disease.

explanation.key_explanation: ABCA3 localizes to lamellar bodies in alveolar type II cells and transports phospholipids needed for normal surfactant assembly. Biallelic loss-of-function variants therefore impair lamellar-body surfactant lipid packaging and can cause severe respiratory disease in term newborns.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Clearance of phosphate from the alveolar space by a sodium-phosphate cotransporter'. It is not selected because it does not account for a term neonate with severe inherited surfactant dysfunction, abnormal lamellar bodies, and biallelic ABCA3 loss; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. ABCA3 localizes to lamellar bodies in alveolar type II cells and transports phospholipids needed for normal surfactant assembly. Biallelic loss-of-function variants therefore impair lamellar-body surfactant lipid packaging and can cause severe respiratory disease in term newborns.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Apical chloride secretion by airway epithelial CFTR channels'. It is not selected because it does not account for a term neonate with severe inherited surfactant dysfunction, abnormal lamellar bodies, and biallelic ABCA3 loss; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Proteolytic activation of surfactant protein C after secretion'. It is not selected because it does not account for a term neonate with severe inherited surfactant dysfunction, abnormal lamellar bodies, and biallelic ABCA3 loss; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Assembly of elastic fibers in the pulmonary interstitium'. It is not selected because it does not account for a term neonate with severe inherited surfactant dysfunction, abnormal lamellar bodies, and biallelic ABCA3 loss; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.

explanation.educational_objective: Know that ABCA3 transports surfactant phospholipids into lamellar bodies of type II pneumocytes and that loss of function causes inherited surfactant dysfunction.

item.vignette: An 8-year-old boy is evaluated for severe short stature. Testing shows growth hormone deficiency and central hypothyroidism. At age 15, he fails to enter puberty and has low LH and FSH despite low testosterone. Follow-up in early adulthood shows a low morning cortisol with an inappropriately low ACTH concentration. MRI shows a small anterior pituitary without optic-nerve or midline brain abnormalities.
item.lead_in: Which genetic defect best explains this evolving endocrine phenotype?
item.tested_construct: PROP1 loss is a major genetic cause of combined pituitary hormone deficiency, typically affecting GH and TSH and later gonadotropins; ACTH deficiency can emerge over time.

explanation.key_explanation: The progressive combination of GH/TSH deficiency, later hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and eventual ACTH deficiency is characteristic of PROP1-related combined pituitary hormone deficiency. POU1F1 defects do not typically abolish LH/FSH, and isolated GHRHR or TBX19 defects do not explain the multi-lineage pattern.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'HESX1 loss of function'. It is not selected because it does not account for progressive loss of several anterior-pituitary lineages including GH/TSH, gonadotropins, and later ACTH without a syndromic midline defect; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'POU1F1 loss of function'. It is not selected because it does not account for progressive loss of several anterior-pituitary lineages including GH/TSH, gonadotropins, and later ACTH without a syndromic midline defect; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'GHRHR loss of function'. It is not selected because it does not account for progressive loss of several anterior-pituitary lineages including GH/TSH, gonadotropins, and later ACTH without a syndromic midline defect; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'TBX19 loss of function'. It is not selected because it does not account for progressive loss of several anterior-pituitary lineages including GH/TSH, gonadotropins, and later ACTH without a syndromic midline defect; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. The progressive combination of GH/TSH deficiency, later hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and eventual ACTH deficiency is characteristic of PROP1-related combined pituitary hormone deficiency. POU1F1 defects do not typically abolish LH/FSH, and isolated GHRHR or TBX19 defects do not explain the multi-lineage pattern.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize PROP1-related combined pituitary hormone deficiency as a progressive, multi-lineage anterior pituitary disorder that can evolve from GH/TSH deficiency to gonadotropin and sometimes ACTH deficiency.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: FSH receptor resistance causing hypergonadotropic ovarian failure

item.vignette: A 17-year-old girl is evaluated for primary amenorrhea and incomplete breast development. She has normal female external genitalia, a uterus, and a 46,XX karyotype. Serum FSH is 72 mIU/mL and LH is 31 mIU/mL; estradiol is low. Pelvic ultrasonography shows small ovaries containing multiple small follicles without a dominant follicle. Her mother is unaffected, and her parents are first cousins.
item.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this patient's findings?

options.B: Ovarian resistance due to an inactivating FSH-receptor variant

item.tested_construct: Inactivating FSHR variants cause gonadotropin resistance with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism/ovarian failure and impaired follicular maturation in 46,XX individuals.

explanation.key_explanation: Markedly elevated gonadotropins with low estradiol establish primary gonadal resistance/failure rather than hypothalamic GnRH deficiency. Inactivating FSHR variants specifically impair follicular maturation and can cause primary amenorrhea with small follicles that fail to mature.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Congenital GnRH-receptor deficiency'. It is not selected because it does not account for a 46,XX patient with primary amenorrhea, high FSH/LH, low estradiol, and follicles that fail to mature despite preserved Müllerian anatomy; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Markedly elevated gonadotropins with low estradiol establish primary gonadal resistance/failure rather than hypothalamic GnRH deficiency. Inactivating FSHR variants specifically impair follicular maturation and can cause primary amenorrhea with small follicles that fail to mature.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for a 46,XX patient with primary amenorrhea, high FSH/LH, low estradiol, and follicles that fail to mature despite preserved Müllerian anatomy; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Aromatase deficiency'. It is not selected because it does not account for a 46,XX patient with primary amenorrhea, high FSH/LH, low estradiol, and follicles that fail to mature despite preserved Müllerian anatomy; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes '17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency'. blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: IGF1R loss causing IGF-I resistance and impaired receptor signaling

item.vignette: A 13-year-old girl was born markedly small for gestational age and has persistent severe postnatal short stature and microcephaly. Serum growth hormone is normal to high and serum IGF-1 is markedly elevated for age. Genetic testing identifies a biallelic pathogenic variant in IGF1R. Patient fibroblasts show reduced response to exogenous IGF-1.
item.lead_in: Which signaling abnormality most directly explains this patient's growth failure?

options.A: Failure of growth-hormone receptor activation of JAK2 and STAT5
options.B: Reduced hepatic synthesis of IGF-1 after growth-hormone stimulation
options.C: Failure to form the circulating IGF-1/IGFBP-3/acid-labile-subunit ternary complex
options.D: Reduced IGF-1 receptor autophosphorylation and downstream signaling despite abundant ligand
options.E: Reduced pulsatile secretion of growth hormone from pituitary somatotrophs

item.tested_construct: IGF1R loss causes target-tissue resistance to IGF-1, often with prenatal and postnatal growth failure and elevated IGF-1; receptor autophosphorylation and downstream signaling are impaired.

explanation.key_explanation: Elevated IGF-1 despite severe prenatal and postnatal growth failure indicates resistance at the IGF-1 receptor rather than failure to synthesize ligand. Pathogenic IGF1R variants reduce receptor activation/autophosphorylation and downstream signaling in target tissues.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Failure of growth-hormone receptor activation of JAK2 and STAT5'. It is not selected because it does not account for severe pre- and postnatal growth failure with high IGF-1 and a pathogenic IGF1R variant demonstrating target-tissue resistance; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'Reduced hepatic synthesis of IGF-1 after growth-hormone stimulation'. It is not selected because it does not account for severe pre- and postnatal growth failure with high IGF-1 and a pathogenic IGF1R variant demonstrating target-tissue resistance; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Failure to form the circulating IGF-1/IGFBP-3/acid-labile-subunit ternary complex'. It is not selected because it does not account for severe pre- and postnatal growth failure with high IGF-1 and a pathogenic IGF1R variant demonstrating target-tissue resistance; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Elevated IGF-1 despite severe prenatal and postnatal growth failure indicates resistance at the IGF-1 receptor rather than failure to synthesize ligand. Pathogenic IGF1R variants reduce receptor activation/autophosphorylation and downstream signaling in target tissues.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Reduced pulsatile secretion of growth hormone from pituitary somatotrophs'. It is not selected because it does not account for severe pre- and postnatal growth failure with high IGF-1 and a pathogenic IGF1R variant demonstrating target-tissue resistance; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: MRAP-dependent trafficking of the ACTH receptor MC2R

item.vignette: A 9-month-old infant has recurrent fasting hypoglycemia and diffuse hyperpigmentation. Serum cortisol is very low and ACTH is markedly elevated. Sodium, potassium, plasma renin activity, and aldosterone are normal. Sequencing of MC2R shows no pathogenic variant, but the infant is homozygous for a loss-of-function variant in MRAP.
item.lead_in: Which molecular effect most directly causes this patient's cortisol deficiency?

options.A: Failure of the ACTH receptor MC2R to traffic efficiently from the endoplasmic reticulum to the cell surface
options.B: Failure to transport cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane
options.C: Loss of 21-hydroxylase activity in the adrenal cortex
options.D: Loss of aldosterone synthase activity in the zona glomerulosa
options.E: Constitutive activation of the glucocorticoid receptor in hypothalamic neurons

item.tested_construct: MRAP is an accessory protein required for normal trafficking and function of the ACTH receptor MC2R; loss causes familial glucocorticoid deficiency type 2 with ACTH resistance and usually preserved mineralocorticoids.

explanation.key_explanation: MRAP interacts with MC2R and is required for efficient receptor trafficking to the plasma membrane. MRAP loss therefore produces adrenal ACTH resistance, low cortisol, high ACTH, hyperpigmentation, and classically preserved mineralocorticoid secretion.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. MRAP interacts with MC2R and is required for efficient receptor trafficking to the plasma membrane. MRAP loss therefore produces adrenal ACTH resistance, low cortisol, high ACTH, hyperpigmentation, and classically preserved mineralocorticoid secretion.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'Failure to transport cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane'. It is not selected because it does not account for isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with very high ACTH, preserved mineralocorticoids, normal MC2R coding sequence, and biallelic MRAP loss; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Loss of 21-hydroxylase activity in the adrenal cortex'. It is not selected because it does not account for isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with very high ACTH, preserved mineralocorticoids, normal MC2R coding sequence, and biallelic MRAP loss; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Loss of aldosterone synthase activity in the zona glomerulosa'. It is not selected because it does not account for isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with very high ACTH, preserved mineralocorticoids, normal MC2R coding sequence, and biallelic MRAP loss; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Constitutive activation of the glucocorticoid receptor in hypothalamic neurons'. It is not selected because it does not account for isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with very high ACTH, preserved mineralocorticoids, normal MC2R coding sequence, and biallelic MRAP loss; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.

explanation.educational_objective: Know that MRAP is required for MC2R trafficking/function and that MRAP loss causes familial glucocorticoid deficiency with isolated ACTH resistance.

evidence_map.claim: Correct. MRAP interacts with MC2R and is required for efficient receptor trafficking to the plasma membrane. MRAP loss therefore produces adrenal ACTH resistance, low cortisol, high ACTH, hyperpigmentation, and classically preserved mineralocorticoid secretion.

internal_content_path: Primary adrenal insufficiency with syndromic autonomic/neurologic disease

item.vignette: A 15-year-old boy has progressive dysphagia and recurrent vomiting. Barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus with distal “bird-beak” narrowing. His parents report that he has never produced normal tears when crying. Examination shows hyperpigmentation and decreased ankle reflexes. Morning cortisol is low, ACTH is markedly elevated, and aldosterone is normal.
item.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this patient's findings?

options.B: Familial glucocorticoid deficiency due to MRAP loss
options.C: Triple-A (Allgrove) syndrome due to AAAS/ALADIN dysfunction

item.tested_construct: Triple-A (Allgrove) syndrome is an autosomal-recessive AAAS disorder characterized by alacrima, achalasia, ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, and often progressive neurologic dysfunction.

explanation.key_explanation: The triad of alacrima, achalasia, and ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency is diagnostic of triple-A syndrome; neurologic manifestations such as peripheral neuropathy are common. AAAS encodes ALADIN, a nuclear-pore-complex protein.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1'. It is not selected because it does not account for the defining combination of lifelong alacrima, achalasia, ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, and peripheral neurologic findings; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'Familial glucocorticoid deficiency due to MRAP loss'. It is not selected because it does not account for the defining combination of lifelong alacrima, achalasia, ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, and peripheral neurologic findings; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. The triad of alacrima, achalasia, and ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency is diagnostic of triple-A syndrome; neurologic manifestations such as peripheral neuropathy are common. AAAS encodes ALADIN, a nuclear-pore-complex protein.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B'. It is not selected because it does not account for the defining combination of lifelong alacrima, achalasia, ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, and peripheral neurologic findings; the complete genotype/phenotype and mechanistic pattern supports the keyed mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy'.
